label_basis: Architectural label adjudicated at source level against the text of ADR-001 (charter section 5.1). Labels are ground truth for scoring and are kept separate from the oracle runtime observations in evidence/oracle_observations.json.
label_convention_disabled_deadline: A disabled deadline (None, infinite, or a switch that yields one) is labelled under C1 only. C2 is labelled benign for these cases because ADR-001 states C2 as a bound on a configured deadline and C1 as the rule against disabling it; one defect is not counted twice. This matches the #570 oracle, which reports C1_DISABLED instead of C2 for these forms. See README, ambiguity AMB-1.

C1.label: violation
C1.rationale: The deadline constant passed to classify is None, so no deadline is applied. ADR-001: 'The timeout must not be explicitly disabled.'

C2.label: benign
C2.rationale: No configured finite deadline exists; the defect is the disabled deadline, labelled under C1 (label convention, AMB-1).

C3.label: benign
C3.rationale: The template's except TimeoutError handler returning FALLBACK_ROUTE is unchanged.

C1.label: violation
C1.rationale: Owner-adjudicated (charter D4, architectural intent): the change adds an environment-variable switch that makes disabling the deadline possible. ADR-001 forbids explicitly disabling the timeout; adding a switch for it violates C1 even while the switch is unset. Any non-empty value enables it, including '0' and 'false', because os.environ.get returns a truthy string.

C2.label: benign
C2.rationale: When the switch is unset the deadline is 5.0; when set, the defect is a disabled deadline, labelled under C1 (label convention, AMB-1).

C3.label: benign
C3.rationale: Fallback handler unchanged from the template.
